title: State Department travel advisory levels by update date, from Wayback captures of its RSS
description: One row per advisory update (country, date updated, level) as State's advisories RSS showed it in an Internet Archive capture. For replaying triage's advisory notices (kind advisory) against Access Now's 2025 shutdowns.

sources.name: US State Department travel advisories RSS, as captured by the Internet Archive
sources.attribution: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Consular Affairs (travel.state.gov); captures by the Internet Archive Wayback Machine

sources.name: US State Department travel advisory pages, as captured by the Internet Archive
sources.attribution: U.S. Department of State, Bureau of Consular Affairs (travel.state.gov); captures by the Internet Archive Wayback Machine

differences: Live Cordon reads State's JSON (cadataapi.state.gov), which carries the update time; the RSS carries the date only, so every row is day precision.
An update that appeared and was replaced between two captures is missed.
Tier is derived the way Cordon marks it (level changed in the 30 days before), not read from a stored change log.
Departure posture (kind posture, read from the advisory text) is not rebuilt.
Gaza and the West Bank are State's combined Israel, West Bank and Gaza advisory, copied to place PS.

biases: Levels are exact on the day of each update; the risk is a missed update between captures, flagged capture-gap on the row that followed.
A 'reissued after periodic review without changes' notice carries a new date at the same level; triage reads it as not raised.
The Archive's captures are irregular and thin in autumn 2025.

row_schema.first_seen: capture time that first showed the row, UTC
